title: Authorised Push Payment and Investment Scams
summary: How criminals persuade customers to send money themselves, from impersonation and romance scams to fake investment platforms, and the points at which firms can intervene.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How criminals persuade customers to send money themselves, from impersonation and romance scams to fake investment platforms, and the points at which firms can intervene.
Learning Objectives: Recognise the stages and psychology of authorised push payment scams
Identify investment, crypto-asset and impersonation scam patterns
Map intervention points across the payment journey
Syllabus: Impersonation, purchase, romance and invoice redirection scams
Investment and crypto-asset scams, cloned firms and fake platforms
Social engineering, coaching and why customers override warnings
Case studies: tracing a scam from first contact to cash-out
Intended Audience: Fraud prevention, fraud operations and investigations teams
Payments operations, customer service and complaints staff who handle suspected fraud cases
Compliance, financial crime and risk staff, and managers accountable for fraud outcomes
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of fraud, payments operations or financial crime compliance is helpful. No technical background in data analytics is required.
Core Reading: FATF, Opportunities and Challenges of New Technologies for AML/CFT (2021)
G20/OECD High-Level Principles on Financial Consumer Protection (2022)
CPMI, Fast Payments: Enhancing the Speed and Availability of Retail Payments (2016)
